methodology_note: Study units were derived from the compact R packet and verified against canonical TOC OCR and targeted body OCR for pdf1455-1494. The canonical TOC is one column, but toc_inventory.json silently omitted the printed parent headings 'Approach to the Respiratory Patient' and 'Sleep-Related Breathing Disorders'; attached the former's children to Acronyms; anchored Airway Disease at R3 instead of its printed/body-confirmed R7; mis-parented Pulmonary Vasculitis and Pulmonary Edema beneath Pulmonary Embolism; and mis-parented sleep topics beneath Neoplasms. Body verification also recovered a substantial Arterial Blood Gases section and four named ILD subsections absent beneath broad inventory nodes. Exact body headings and page boundaries were used where available; no respiratory topic was added from medical knowledge. Cross-reference-only nodes remain explicitly cross-disciplinary, and References are excluded as bibliography.

study_units.title: Respirology Acronyms
study_units.structural_rationale: The chapter-opening acronym glossary is retained as one reference unit; it is not fragmented into individual abbreviations.

study_units.title: Basic Respiratory Anatomy
study_units.structural_rationale: Canonical TOC OCR and the R2 body confirm that Basic Anatomy Review belongs under the omitted parent heading 'Approach to the Respiratory Patient', not under Acronyms. The missing parent is preserved with the established UNCATALOGUED convention.

study_units.title: Differential Diagnosis of Common Respiratory Presentations
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation on R3 shows a coherent presentation-based approach (including dyspnea and chest pain tables); it is one learner-facing diagnostic unit.

study_units.title: Basic Pulmonary Function Test Interpretation
study_units.structural_rationale: Body heading and content on R4 confirm a single generalist-level unit on obstructive/restrictive patterns, lung volumes, flows, and diffusion capacity.

study_units.title: Basic Chest Radiograph Patterns
study_units.structural_rationale: The R5 body presents one compact pattern-recognition table and a Medical Imaging cross-reference; it remains a single basic interpretation unit.

study_units.title: Arterial Blood Gases, Acid-Base Status, and Hypoxemia
study_units.structural_rationale: A substantial body-confirmed heading omitted from toc_inventory.json spans R5-R6 and integrates ABG interpretation, respiratory acid-base disorders, A-a gradient, hypoxemia mechanisms, and V/Q mismatch; these form one coherent foundational unit.

study_units.title: Pneumonia (Respiratory Cross-Reference)
study_units.structural_rationale: The R body contains only a cross-reference to Pediatrics, so the node is retained without reconstructing pneumonia content from medical knowledge.

study_units.title: Asthma
study_units.structural_rationale: The body-confirmed Asthma heading and its contiguous assessment and management content form one clinical topic.

study_units.title: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
study_units.structural_rationale: The body-confirmed COPD material spans diagnosis, stable disease, exacerbation, prevention, rehabilitation, and prognosis; generic subheadings remain integrated as one disease unit.

study_units.title: Bronchiectasis
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation on R12 supports one coherent condition-level unit.

study_units.title: Cystic Fibrosis
study_units.structural_rationale: The body-confirmed topic begins on R12 and continues through R13; multisystem features and pulmonary care remain one condition-level unit.

study_units.title: General Approach to Interstitial Lung Disease
study_units.structural_rationale: The section's definition, physiology, etiologic taxonomy, clinical features, imaging, PFT findings, and initial investigation approach are a coherent generalist framework distinct from its named disease examples.

study_units.title: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
study_units.structural_rationale: The broad source node contains a body-confirmed standalone IPF heading on R15; the disease is kept as one unit while rare idiopathic ILD classifications remain contextual.

study_units.title: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis
study_units.structural_rationale: The broad Known Etiologic Agents node contains a substantial body-confirmed HP heading with exposure-specific assessment and management, supporting a distinct learner-facing unit.

study_units.title: Sarcoidosis
study_units.structural_rationale: The R16-R17 body gives sarcoidosis a standalone multi-system clinical section, justifying a source-traceable split from the broad Known Etiologic Agents node.

study_units.title: Pneumoconioses and Occupational Fibrotic Lung Disease
study_units.structural_rationale: A body-confirmed pneumoconioses section spans R17-R18 and compares asbestos-, silica-, and coal-related disease; the shared occupational assessment framework supports one grouped unit.

study_units.title: Drug- and Treatment-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease
study_units.structural_rationale: The R18 body contains a standalone heading and compact culprit-pattern table, supporting a separate recognition-focused unit without expanding into specialist histopathologic classification.

study_units.title: Pulmonary Hypertension
study_units.structural_rationale: Pulmonary Vascular Disease opens directly into a single substantive Pulmonary Hypertension topic; section and child are combined.

study_units.title: Pulmonary Embolism
study_units.structural_rationale: Canonical TOC and body headings confirm Pulmonary Embolism as a standalone three-page section. The inventory's apparent child attachment of later R23 topics is a structural extraction defect and is not preserved.

study_units.title: Pulmonary Vasculitis and Alveolar Hemorrhage
study_units.structural_rationale: The R23 body confirms Pulmonary Vasculitis as a standalone sibling topic after Pulmonary Embolism, not part of the PE section; the unit emphasizes recognition of pulmonary-renal and hemorrhagic presentations.

study_units.title: Pulmonary Edema (Cardiology Cross-Reference)
study_units.structural_rationale: The body contains only a Cardiology cross-reference. It is retained as a cross-discipline node without reconstructing content.

study_units.title: Mediastinal Masses (Thoracic Surgery Cross-Reference)
source_hierarchy_path: R.S06 (Diseases of the Mediastinum and Pleura)
study_units.structural_rationale: The main body is a General and Thoracic Surgery cross-reference with only a compact compartment mnemonic; no specialist staging content is inferred.

study_units.title: Mediastinitis
source_hierarchy_path: R.S06 (Diseases of the Mediastinum and Pleura)
study_units.structural_rationale: The R23 body provides a distinct acute mediastinitis presentation and urgent treatment framework, supporting one recognition-and-referral unit.

study_units.title: Pleural Effusion, Parapneumonic Effusion, and Empyema
source_hierarchy_path: R.S06 (Diseases of the Mediastinum and Pleura)
R.S06.T03-T05 (Pleural Effusions; Complicated Parapneumonic Effusion; Empyema)
study_units.structural_rationale: Pleural fluid assessment on R24-R25 and the linked parapneumonic/empyema complications on R25-R26 form one coherent diagnostic and escalation pathway; the two complication nodes are brief Thoracic Surgery cross-references.

study_units.title: Atelectasis (Thoracic Surgery Cross-Reference)
source_hierarchy_path: R.S06 (Diseases of the Mediastinum and Pleura)
study_units.structural_rationale: The chapter provides only a Thoracic Surgery cross-reference, so this remains a minimal recognition unit.

study_units.title: Pneumothorax and Tension Pneumothorax
source_hierarchy_path: R.S06 (Diseases of the Mediastinum and Pleura)
study_units.structural_rationale: Although the main heading cross-refers to Thoracic Surgery, the R26 body contains a substantial emergency recognition and initial-action panel, supporting a distinct generalist unit.

study_units.title: Asbestos-Related Pleural Disease and Mesothelioma
source_hierarchy_path: R.S06 (Diseases of the Mediastinum and Pleura)
study_units.structural_rationale: The adjacent topics share one exposure-based diagnostic pathway and pleural malignancy distinction; grouping avoids artificial fragmentation while preserving both source nodes.

study_units.title: Hypoxemic and Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure
study_units.structural_rationale: The section defines respiratory failure and contrasts two physiologic types within one integrated assessment, oxygenation, and ventilation pathway; they remain one generalist emergency unit.

study_units.title: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
study_units.structural_rationale: ARDS has its own body-confirmed definition, diagnostic criteria, complications, and management principles, supporting a separate recognition-and-act unit.

study_units.title: Lung Cancer (Thoracic Surgery Cross-Reference)
study_units.structural_rationale: The R chapter supplies only a Thoracic Surgery cross-reference; this unit preserves generalist recognition and referral scope without importing staging detail.

study_units.title: Solitary Pulmonary Nodule (Imaging and Surgery Cross-Reference)
source_hierarchy_path: R.S08.T02 (Approach to the Solitary Pulmonary Nodule)
study_units.structural_rationale: The R body contains only Medical Imaging and Thoracic Surgery cross-references; no nodule algorithm or threshold is reconstructed here.

study_units.title: Sleep-Related Hypoventilation Syndromes
source_hierarchy_path: R.S08.T03 (Hypoventilation Syndromes; mis-parented under Neoplasms in inventory)
study_units.structural_rationale: Canonical TOC and R29 body confirm an omitted Sleep-Related Breathing Disorders parent after Neoplasms. Hypoventilation Syndromes is restored beneath that parent as a distinct physiologic syndrome unit.

study_units.title: Sleep Apnea
source_hierarchy_path: R.S08.T04 (Sleep Apnea; mis-parented under Neoplasms in inventory)
study_units.structural_rationale: R29-R30 body headings support one unit covering sleep testing plus obstructive and central sleep apnea at generalist recognition and initial-management depth.

study_units.title: Intensive Care Unit Basics
study_units.structural_rationale: The short section frames indications for intensive monitoring and stabilization; it is retained as contextual supporting knowledge.

study_units.title: Critical Care Lines and Catheters
study_units.structural_rationale: The source focuses on device sites, hemodynamic measurements, and pulmonary artery catheter details; procedural technique is specialist-level and kept in one bounded unit.

study_units.title: Recognition of Multisystem Organ Failure
study_units.structural_rationale: The source is a cross-system comparison table that points to other chapters; it supports contextual recognition without duplicating definitive organ-specific management.

study_units.title: Shock: Recognition and Initial Stabilization
study_units.structural_rationale: The R32 body provides an integrated classification, examination, and initial treatment framework; detailed disease-specific therapy remains outside this unit.

study_units.title: Sepsis and Septic Shock
study_units.structural_rationale: The body-confirmed sepsis section spans R32-R34 and integrates recognition of organ dysfunction, shock, initial resuscitation, antimicrobials, and source control as one urgent-care unit.

study_units.title: Common Respiratory and ICU Medications
study_units.structural_rationale: The section is a dense dose/indication/adverse-effect reference table. At scope stage it is retained as reference material and does not freeze changing doses, inhaler sequences, or antimicrobial regimens.

study_units.title: Landmark Respirology Trials
study_units.structural_rationale: The section summarizes historical trials across ARDS, asthma, COPD, ILD, PE, OSA, and intensive care; individual trial minutiae are reference-only rather than independent study units.
